evidence.observation: Core3D exports distinct database nouns for a linear dimension, dimension point, and dimension projection line. RTTI also exposes pseudo-attribute readers for POS on DIMPPT/DIMPLI and PPOS/WBOX on LINDIM.
evidence.implication: E3D persists semantic dimension structure separately from its rendered lines. The web port should keep semantic anchors and layout intent as domain data, then derive render geometry.

evidence.observation: The dimension checker resolves first/previous/next/last dimension points, obtains dimension and projection directions, reads the active view direction, and rejects degenerate combinations before drawing.
evidence.implication: Validation is a first-class boundary and must run before layout. It must return stable, user-visible error codes instead of silently drawing a fallback.

evidence.observation: DMCHEK reports projection-line parallel to dimension-line, projection-line parallel to view, and dimension-line parallel to view. Cross-product magnitude uses 0.00005 as a near-parallel threshold; a 2D projected determinant check uses 0.0025.
evidence.implication: The port needs separate dimensionDirection, projectionDirection, and transient viewDirection inputs plus deterministic near-parallel tolerances.

evidence.observation: For the linear-dimension database type, DMLDAT reads or derives both the projection-line direction and dimension-line direction, normalizes vectors, and rejects unexpected types.
evidence.implication: Measured direction and projection/extension direction are different concepts. They must not share one field in the web domain model.

evidence.observation: DPTPOS switches by dimension-point type, follows stored references and attributes, and computes a current 3D position rather than relying only on a frozen coordinate.
evidence.implication: A web dimension anchor needs both a design-coordinate snapshot and a resolvable semantic reference. Model-version refresh should re-resolve in batches and retain the snapshot on failure.

evidence.observation: DPTDIR derives a direction from referenced geometry or stored vectors, supports reversal, then projects the result through DMPROJ.
evidence.implication: Direction snaps require semantic ownership, orientation, and an explicit reversed sense. A raw world vector alone is insufficient for durable projected dimensions.

evidence.observation: DMPROJ computes dot(axis, vector), subtracts the axial component, and normalizes the remainder: normalize(vector - axis * dot(axis, vector)).
evidence.implication: The E3D-compatible frame kernel can be implemented as a small pure function with direct structural golden tests.

evidence.observation: Angles whose angle/90 ratio is within 0.01 of an integer are snapped to the corresponding multiple of 90 degrees.
evidence.implication: Near-orthogonal input should have an explicit snap policy. The observed threshold is equivalent to approximately 0.9 degrees, pending runtime confirmation.

evidence.observation: DOFFS stores a scalar offset. For the linear-dimension type it derives the scalar with dot products against dimension geometry; other supported types can use point distance. SAVE/RESTORE surrounds the operation.
evidence.implication: Offset is durable design-space placement intent. Pointer movement must be projected onto a selected dimension frame before commit, and cancel must restore the pre-edit state.

evidence.observation: Dimension-point creation is a staged command process. It initializes a point type, captures cursor or referenced-element state, validates the point type, creates a child database element, applies semantic attachment attributes, and can abort or restore.
evidence.implication: The web creation flow should remain an explicit typed session with pick, direction/frame, placement, ready, commit, cancel, and back-step states. Numeric E3D noun hashes must not be copied.

evidence.observation: CHAIN persists a boolean chain mode through SAVE/RESTORE and validates the active dimension type before accepting the change.
evidence.implication: Chain mode should be represented as ordered anchors sharing one baseline and placement frame, not as unrelated two-point dimensions.

evidence.observation: DPTANG selects among multiple dimension-point angle modes and DTRAD reads/writes radial values or referenced radius attributes. Both use staged action dispatch and abort on invalid state.
evidence.implication: Angular plane/radius placement and radial label/leader placement need dedicated session states. Exact UI mode mapping remains a runtime-capture item.

evidence.observation: Dimension text formatting is centralized. The routine applies unit-dependent conversion and precision, including observed divisors 25.4, 304.8, 10, and 1000, and has separate angular formatting paths.
evidence.implication: Formatting must stay outside persisted geometry. Exact suffixes, rounding, trailing-zero, feet/inch, and angle presentation require E3D runtime goldens before changing the web format policy.

evidence.observation: The structural grid path requires at least two points, iterates adjacent point pairs, computes D3_Point distance, formats through DES_Units, draws vector/extrusion text, filled arrow triangles, and wire lines.
evidence.implication: The existing batched Three.js scene painter is a suitable presentation target. Grid-derived dimensions should enter it as read-only external records.

evidence.observation: The manager is enabled/reentrancy guarded, reacts to draw-list additions and deletions, limits automatic work to GRIDPL/GRIDCY, clears prior annotations, and rebuilds for a selected view.
evidence.implication: Automatic grid dimensions need their own invalidation-driven external source. They must not enter user history, persistence, authorship, or review edit permissions.

evidence.observation: Grid annotation separates source-line collection, dimension construction, and view-aware text transformation. It renders through SGL attributes and transformed scene geometry.
evidence.implication: Source collection, pure layout, and scene painting should remain separate ports in plant3d-web.

limitations: Only the plant3 Core3D.dll IDB contains the rendering and interaction implementation used for this evidence set.
The connected plant210/core.dll and plant3/core.dll IDBs expose DBE_Dimension and unit-expression symbols but do not provide a second Core3D implementation for cross-version parity.
Numeric noun and attribute hash values were intentionally not assigned product meanings unless a named symbol or diagnostic string supported the mapping.
Static analysis cannot establish exact UI wording, visual constants, pointer-event ordering, or every command-case mapping; those remain runtime golden-capture requirements.
